Victime revendiquée par le groupe de rançongiciel HYFLOCK.

Pays : CM.

Secteur : Government & Defense.

The core conclusion has already completed an analysis of the entire database's data volume sorted by table. It can be confirmed that this is a massive database containing over 6 million records, including nearly 1.35 million historical personnel records (HISTO_RECIP) and nearly 2.41 million core operation audits/history records (HISTO_OR). More seriously, the TMOUCHARD table contains nearly 1 million records—in French, 'Mouchard' means 'spy/listener/log monitor,' which indicates that the system's core activity audit logs have also fallen into the hands of the attacker. Below is a deep security breakdown of the non-empty tables sorted by data: 1. Precise Quantitative Analysis of Core Affected Assets By doing this, the attacker has effectively ranked the database's assets by value. The following types of data are in extremely high-risk status: 1) Core identities and historical records (totaling about 1.6 million+) • RECIPIENDAIRE (160,920 records) & DISTINCTION (161,481 records): Current roster of awarded/declared military and political personnel. • HISTO_RECIP (1,349,243 records): This is the largest core asset, containing detailed birth/death records, career histories, files, or background information for over 1.34 million historical personnel. • FGRADE_ARME (6,542 records): Military rank and branch correspondence, used to precisely identify high-value targets (such as generals and senior special forces officers). 2) System core audit logs have been 'reverse-forensicated' (nearly 1 million records) • TMOUCHARD (999,037 records): In French business systems, 'Mouchard' usually refers to backdoor logs, user activity tracking logs, or security audit tables. • Severe consequence: The attacker stole nearly a million audit logs, which means they didn't just take the data—they also learned the system administrators' routine checks, login times, and frequently accessed assets. items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

The U.S arm of international hearing aid company Amplifon has been notifying customers about a data breach early this year that included medical information.

International healthcare company Amplifon said thousands of its U.S. customers had their Social Security numbers and medical information stolen during a cyberattack in February.

The Milan, Italy, company pairs patients in need of hearing aids and auditory assistance with device providers and services.

Amplifon began notifying state regulators of a data breach last week, telling Texas officials that 85,804 people were impacted by the security incident in addition to 1,027 people in Vermont. The company also filed breach notices in California .

In a breach notice on its U.S. website , Amplifon said it initially discovered suspicious activity on February 11, with an investigation later revealing the hackers had access to company files between January 18 and February 8.

The stolen data includes names, driver’s licenses, state IDs, medical information, health insurance data and financial information.

No hacking group has taken credit for the incident as of Monday.

Unknown attackers used compromised identity and access management (IAM) credentials associated with Qubole's AWS account to access customer AWS environments, stealing secrets and other sensitive data from S3 buckets. The supply-chain attack abused this third-party, cross-account trust relationship. Google’s cloud-security shop Wiz declined to tell us how many organizations were affected, but called it a “broad, opportunistic supply chain campaign” that hit “multiple” customer environments. “Because many organizations left trust policies active even after deprecating the platform, the attacker was able to successfully assume integration roles, enumerate cloud resources, harvest secrets, and siphon data,” the researchers told The Register in an emailed response to questions.
